Version Control and Branch Management版本控制与分支管理

[图示]

Chapter opener illustration: a bird silhouette (decorative).

章首装饰插图：一只鸟的剪影（纯装饰，已省略）。

Written by Titus Winters

作者：Titus Winters

Edited by Lisa Carey

编辑：Lisa Carey

Perhaps no software engineering tool is quite as universally adopted throughout the industry as version control. One can hardly imagine any software organization larger than a few people that does not rely on a formal Version Control System (VCS) to manage its source code and coordinate activities between engineers.

在整个行业中，或许没有哪种软件工程工具像版本控制那样被普遍采用。几乎无法想象：任何超过几个人的软件组织，会不依赖一个正式的版本控制系统（VCS）来管理源代码、协调工程师之间的工作。

In this chapter, we are going to look at why the use of version control has become such an unambiguous norm in software engineering, and we describe the various possible approaches to version control and branch management, including how we do it at scale across all of Google. We will also examine the pros and cons of various approaches; although we believe everyone should use version control, some version control policies and processes might work better for your organization (or in general) than others. In particular, we find trunk-based development as popularized by DevOps (one repository, no dev branches) to be a particularly scalable policy approach, and we will provide some suggestions as to why that is.

本章中，我们将考察：为什么版本控制的使用会成为软件工程中如此不言自明的规范；并描述版本控制与分支管理的各种可能做法，包括我们如何在整个 Google 大规模地践行。我们还将考察各种做法的优缺点；尽管我们相信人人都应使用版本控制，但某些版本控制政策与流程，对你的组织（或总体而言）可能比另一些更有效。我们特别发现：由 DevOps 推广开来的“基于主干的开发”（trunk-based development，单一仓库、不设开发分支）是一种尤其可扩展的政策取向，我们也会就其原因给出一些建议。

What Is Version Control? · 什么是版本控制？

This section might be a little basic for many readers: use of version control is, after all, fairly ubiquitous. If you want to skip ahead, we suggest jumping to the section Source of Truth on page 334.

本节对许多读者而言可能略偏基础：毕竟版本控制的使用已相当普遍。如果你想跳过，我们建议直接翻到第 334 页的“真相之源”（Source of Truth）一节。

原书第 355 页

A VCS is a system that tracks revisions (versions) of files over time. A VCS maintains some metadata about the set of files being managed, and collectively a copy of the files and metadata is called a repository (repo for short). A VCS helps coordinate the activities of teams by allowing multiple developers to work on the same set of files simultaneously. Early VCSs did this by granting one person at a time the right to edit a file—that style of locking is enough to establish sequencing (an agreed-upon which is newer, an important feature of VCS). More advanced systems ensure that changes to a collection of files submitted at once are treated as a single unit (atomicity when a logical change touches multiple files). Systems like CVS (a popular VCS from the 90s) that did not have this atomicity for a commit were subject to corruption and lost changes. Ensuring atomicity removes the chance of previous changes being overwritten unintentionally, but requires tracking which version was last synced to—at commit time, the commit is rejected if any file in the commit has been modified at head since the last time the local developer synced. Especially in such a change-tracking VCS, a developer's working copy of the managed files will therefore need metadata of its own. Depending on the design of the VCS, this copy of the repository can be a repository itself, or might contain a reduced amount of metadata—such a reduced copy is usually a client or workspace.

VCS 是一种随时间跟踪文件修订（版本）的系统。VCS 会维护关于被管理文件集合的一些元数据；文件与元数据的一份副本合在一起，称为一个仓库（repository，简称 repo）。VCS 通过允许多名开发者同时在同一组文件上工作，来帮助协调团队的活动。早期的 VCS 是这样做的：一次只授予一个人编辑某个文件的权利——这种锁定方式足以确立时序关系（即一个约定好的“哪个更新”，这是 VCS 的一项重要特性）。更先进的系统则保证：一次提交的对一组文件的变更，被当作一个整体对待（当一个逻辑变更涉及多个文件时的原子性）。像 CVS（90 年代流行的一种 VCS）这样不具备提交原子性的系统，容易出现损坏和变更丢失。保证原子性消除了先前变更被无意覆盖的可能，但需要跟踪上次同步到的是哪个版本——在提交时，如果自本地开发者上次同步以来，提交中的任何文件已在主干被修改，该提交就会被拒绝。尤其在这种基于变更跟踪的 VCS 中，开发者对被管理文件的工作副本因此也需要有自己的元数据。根据 VCS 的设计，这份仓库副本本身可以是一个完整仓库，也可能只包含较少的元数据——这种精简副本通常被称为“客户端”或“工作区”。

This seems like a lot of complexity: why is a VCS necessary? What is it about this sort of tool that has allowed it to become one of the few nearly universal tools for software development and software engineering?

这看起来相当复杂：为什么还需要 VCS？究竟是这种工具的什么特质，让它成为软件开发与软件工程中少有的几种几乎普适的工具之一？

Imagine for a moment working without a VCS. For a (very) small group of distributed developers working on a project of limited scope without any understanding of version control, the simplest and lowest-infrastructure solution is to just pass copies of the project back and forth. This works best when edits are nonsimultaneous (people are working in different time zones, or at least with different working hours). If there is any chance for people to not know which version is the most current, we immediately have an annoying problem: tracking which version is the most up to date. Anyone who has attempted to collaborate in a non-networked environment will likely recall the horrors of copying back-and-forth files named Presentation v5 - final - redlines - Josh's version v2. And as we shall see, when there is not a single agreed-upon source of truth, collaboration becomes high friction and error prone.

暂且想象一下在没有 VCS 的情况下工作。对于一个（非常）小的、分布各地的开发者小组，在一个范围有限、且对版本控制毫无概念的项目上，最简单、基础设施成本最低的做法，就是把项目副本传来传去。当编辑不同时发生时（大家在不同时区，或至少工作时间不同），这种方式效果最好。只要存在“大家不知道哪个版本是最新”的可能，我们立刻就有了一个恼人的问题：跟踪哪个版本是最新的。任何在非联网环境中尝试过协作的人，大概都会回忆起那种反复拷贝名为“Presentation v5 - final - redlines - Josh's version v2”的文件的恐怖经历。而正如我们将看到的：当不存在唯一约定好的真相之源时，协作就会变得摩擦巨大、容易出错。

Introducing shared storage requires slightly more infrastructure (getting access to shared storage), but provides an easy and obvious solution. Coordinating work in a shared drive might suffice for a while with a small enough number of people but still requires out-of-band collaboration to avoid overwriting one another's work. Further, working directly in that shared storage means that any development task that does not

引入共享存储需要稍多一些基础设施（获得共享存储的访问权），但提供了一个简单而显然的解决方案。在人数足够少时，在共享网盘里协调工作也许能维持一阵，但仍然需要带外协作，以避免互相覆盖工作。此外，直接在那个共享存储中工作意味着：任何一项不

原书第 356 页

keep the build working continuously will begin to impede everyone on the team—if I am making a change to some part of this system at the same time that you kick off a build, your build will not work. Obviously, this does not scale well.

能让构建持续通过的开发任务，都会开始妨碍团队中的每一个人——如果我正对系统的某个部分做改动，而你同时启动了一次构建，你的构建就跑不起来。显然，这种方式可扩展性很差。

In practice, lack of file locking and lack of merge tracking will inevitably lead to collisions and work being overwritten. Such a system is very likely to introduce out-of-band coordination to decide who is working on any given file. If that file-locking is encoded in software, we have begun reinventing an early-generation version control like RCS (among others). After you realize that granting write permissions a file at a time is too coarse grained and you begin wanting line-level tracking—we are definitely reinventing version control. It seems nearly inevitable that we will want some structured mechanism to govern these collaborations. Because we seem to just be reinventing the wheel in this hypothetical, we might as well use an off-the-shelf tool.

实践中，缺少文件锁定、缺少合并跟踪，将不可避免地导致冲突和工作被覆盖。这样一套系统很可能会引入带外协调，来决定谁在处理哪个文件。如果把那种文件锁定用软件实现出来，我们就已经开始重新发明 RCS 这类早期版本控制了。当你意识到“一次只给一个文件写权限”粒度太粗、并开始想要行级跟踪时——我们就毫无疑问地在重新发明版本控制了。我们几乎不可避免地会想要某种结构化机制来治理这些协作。既然在这个假想场景里我们只是在重复造轮子，那还不如直接用一个现成工具。

Why Is Version Control Important? · 版本控制为什么重要？

While version control is practically ubiquitous now, this was not always the case. The very first VCSs date back to the 1970s (SCCS) and 1980s (RCS)—many years later than the first references to software engineering as a distinct discipline. Teams participated in the multiperson development of multiversion software before the industry had any formal notion of version control. Version control evolved as a response to the novel challenges of digital collaboration. It took decades of evolution and dissemination for reliable, consistent use of version control to evolve into the norm that it is today. So how did it become so important, and, given that it seems like a self-evident solution, why might anyone resist the idea of VCS?

尽管版本控制如今几乎无处不在，但情况并非一直如此。最早的 VCS 可追溯到 1970 年代（SCCS）和 1980 年代（RCS）——比“软件工程”作为一门独立学科被首次提及晚了许多年。在行业还没有任何版本控制的正式概念之前，各团队就已经在参与“多版本软件的多人开发”了。版本控制是为应对数字化协作的新挑战而演进出来的。经过数十年的演进与传播，可靠、一致地使用版本控制才演变为今天这样的规范。那么，它是如何变得如此重要的？而且，既然它看起来是一个不言自明的解决方案，为什么还会有人抵触 VCS 这个概念？

Recall that software engineering is programming integrated over time; we are drawing a distinction (in dimensionality) between the instantaneous production of source code and the act of maintaining that product over time. That basic distinction goes a long way to explaining the importance of, and hesitation toward, VCS: at the most fundamental level, version control is the engineer's primary tool for managing the interplay between raw source and time. We can conceptualize VCS as a way to extend a standard filesystem. A filesystem is a mapping from filename to contents. A VCS extends that to provide a mapping from (filename, time) to contents, along with the metadata necessary to track last sync points and audit history. Version control makes the consideration of time an explicit part of the operation: unnecessary in a program

回想一下：软件工程是随时间整合起来的编程；我们在（维度上）把“瞬时产出源代码”与“随时间维护该产品”区分开来。这个基本区分，很大程度上解释了 VCS 的重要性、以及人们对它的犹豫：在最根本的层面上，版本控制是工程师管理“原始源码与时间之间相互作用”的首要工具。我们可以把 VCS 概念化为对标准文件系统的一种扩展。文件系统是一个从文件名到内容的映射；VCS 把它扩展为提供一个从（文件名，时间）到内容的映射，连同跟踪上次同步点与审计历史所需的元数据。版本控制让“时间”成为操作中显式考虑的一部分：在一个

原书第 357 页

ming task, critical in a software engineering task. In most cases, a VCS also allows for an extra input to that mapping (a branch name) to allow for parallel mappings; thus:

编程任务中它并非必需，但在软件工程任务中它至关重要。在大多数情况下，VCS 还允许给该映射增加一个额外输入（分支名），以支持并行映射；因此：

VCS(filename, time, branch) => file contents

In the default usage, that branch input will have a commonly understood default: we call that head, default, or trunk to denote main branch.

在默认用法中，那个分支输入会有一个被普遍理解的默认值：我们称之为 head、default 或 trunk，用以表示主干分支。

The (minor) remaining hesitation toward consistent use of version control comes almost directly from conflating programming and software engineering—we teach programming, we train programmers, we interview for jobs based on programming problems and techniques. It is perfectly reasonable for a new hire, even at a place like Google, to have little or no experience with code that is worked on by more than one person or for more than a couple weeks. Given that experience and understanding of the problem, version control seems like an alien solution. Version control is solving a problem that our new hire has not necessarily experienced: an undo, not for a single file but for an entire project, adding a lot of complexity for sometimes nonobvious benefits.

对“一致使用版本控制”尚存的那点（轻微）犹豫，几乎直接来自把编程与软件工程混为一谈——我们教编程、培训程序员、并基于编程题目与技巧来面试招聘。一个新员工，即便在 Google 这样的地方，对“由多人协作、或持续超过一两周的代码”几乎没有经验，也是完全合理的。基于那种经验和对问题的理解，版本控制看起来就像一个异己的解决方案。版本控制所解决的，是我们这位新员工未必经历过的问题：不是对单个文件的“撤销”，而是对整个项目的“撤销”——它带来了大量复杂度，而收益有时并不显而易见。

In some software groups, the same result plays out when management views the job of the techies as software development (sit down and write code) rather than software engineering (produce code, keep it working and useful for some extended period). With a mental model of programming as the primary task and little understanding of the interplay between code and the passage of time, it is easy to see something described as go back to a previous version to undo a mistake as a weird, high-overhead luxury.

在某些软件团队中，当管理层把技术人员的工作看作“软件开发”（坐下来写代码）而非“软件工程”（产出代码、并在一段较长时间内保持其可用、有用）时，也会出现同样的结果。在这种把编程当作主要任务、对代码与时间流逝之间相互作用缺乏理解的心智模型下，人们很容易把“回到先前版本以撤销错误”这种描述，看作一种古怪、高开销的奢侈品。

In addition to allowing separate storage and reference to versions over time, version control helps us bridge the gap between single-developer and multideveloper processes. In practical terms, this is why version control is so critical to software engineering, because it allows us to scale up teams and organizations, even though we use it only infrequently as an undo button. Development is inherently a branch-and-merge process, both when coordinating between multiple developers or a single developer at different points in time. A VCS removes the question of which is more recent? Use of modern version control automates error-prone operations like tracking which set of changes have been applied. Version control is how we coordinate between multiple developers and/or multiple points in time.

除了允许随时间对版本进行独立存储与引用之外，版本控制还帮助我们弥合“单开发者流程”与“多开发者流程”之间的鸿沟。从实践意义上说，这正是版本控制对软件工程如此关键的原因：它让我们能够扩大团队与组织规模——哪怕我们很少把它当作“撤销”按钮来用。开发本质上是一个分支—合并过程，无论是在多名开发者之间协调，还是在同一名开发者的不同时间点之间协调。VCS 消除了“哪个更新？”这个问题。使用现代版本控制，把“跟踪已应用了哪一组变更”这类容易出错的操作自动化了。版本控制，就是我们在多名开发者和/或多个时间点之间进行协调的方式。

Because VCS has become so thoroughly embedded in the process of software engineering, even legal and regulatory practices have caught up. VCS allows a formal record of every change to every line of code, which is increasingly necessary for satisfying audit requirements. When mixing between in-house development and appropriate use of third-party sources, VCS helps track provenance and origination for every line of code.

由于 VCS 已经如此彻底地嵌入软件工程流程，连法律与监管实践也随之跟上了。VCS 为每一行代码的每一次变更保留正式记录，这对于满足审计要求日益必要。当在内部开发与恰当地使用第三方来源之间混合时，VCS 有助于跟踪每一行代码的出处与来源。

原书第 358 页

In addition to the technical and regulatory aspects of tracking source over time and handling sync/branch/merge operations, version control triggers some nontechnical changes in behavior. The ritual of committing to version control and producing a commit log is a trigger for a moment of reflection: what have you accomplished since your last commit? Is the source in a state that you are happy with? The moment of introspection associated with committing, writing up a summary, and marking a task complete might have value on its own for many people. The start of the commit process is a perfect time to run through a checklist, run static analyses (see Chapter 20), check test coverage, run tests and dynamic analysis, and so on.

除了随时间跟踪源码、处理同步/分支/合并操作这些技术与监管层面之外，版本控制还会触发一些非技术性的行为改变。向版本控制提交、并生成提交日志这一仪式，是一个让人停下来反思的触发点：自上次提交以来，你完成了什么？源码是否处于你满意的状态？与提交、撰写摘要、把任务标记为完成相关联的那一刻自省，对许多人而言本身就可能有价值。提交流程的开端，正是跑一遍检查清单、运行静态分析（见第 20 章）、检查测试覆盖率、运行测试与动态分析等等的理想时机。

Like any process, version control comes with some overhead: someone must configure and manage your version control system, and individual developers must use it. But make no mistake about it: these can almost always be pretty cheap. Anecdotally, most experienced software engineers will instinctively use version control for any project that lasts more than a day or two, even for a single-developer project. The consistency of that result argues that the trade-off in terms of value (including risk reduction) versus overhead must be a pretty easy one. But we have promised to acknowledge that context matters and to encourage engineering leaders to think for themselves. It is always worth considering alternatives, even on something as fundamental as version control.

与任何流程一样，版本控制也带有一些开销：必须有人配置并管理你的版本控制系统，个体开发者也必须使用它。但请不要误会：这些开销几乎总是相当低廉。根据经验，大多数有经验的软件工程师，对任何持续超过一两天的项目都会本能地使用版本控制，哪怕是单开发者项目。这种结果的一致性表明：在价值（包括风险降低）与开销之间的权衡，必定是相当容易做出的。但我们也承诺过要承认情境很重要、并鼓励工程领导者独立思考。即使是在版本控制这样根本的事情上，也总是值得考虑一下替代方案。

In truth, it is difficult to envision any task that can be considered modern software engineering that does not immediately adopt a VCS. Given that you understand the value and need for version control, you are likely now asking what type of version control you need.

事实上，很难想象有哪项可被视为现代软件工程的任务，会不立即采用 VCS。既然你已理解版本控制的价值与必要性，你现在大概会问：我需要哪种类型的版本控制？

Centralized VCS Versus Distributed VCS · 集中式 VCS 与分布式 VCS

At the most simplistic level, all modern VCSs are equivalent to one another: so long as your system has a notion of atomically committing changes to a batch of files, everything else is just UI. You could build the same general semantics (not workflow) of any modern VCS out of another one and a pile of simple shell scripts. Thus, arguing about which VCS is better is primarily a matter of user experience—the core functionality is the same, the differences come in user experience, naming, edge-case features, and performance. Choosing a VCS is like choosing a filesystem format: when choosing among a modern-enough format, the differences are fairly minor, and the more important question by far is the content you fill that system with and the way you use it. However, major architectural differences in VCSs can make configuration, policy, and scaling decisions easier or more difficult, so it is important to be aware of the big architectural differences, chiefly the decision between centralized or decentralized.

在最简化的层面上，所有现代 VCS 彼此等价：只要你的系统具备“把一批文件的变更原子化提交”的概念，其余一切都只是 UI。你完全可以用另一个 VCS 加一堆简单 shell 脚本，构建出任何现代 VCS 的通用语义（而非工作流）。因此，争论哪个 VCS“更好”，主要是用户体验层面的事——核心功能是相同的，差异体现在用户体验、命名、边角功能和性能上。选择 VCS 就像选择文件系统格式：在一个足够现代的格式之间做选择时，差异相当微小；远为重要的问题，是你往这个系统里填充什么内容、以及你如何使用它。然而，VCS 之间的重大架构差异，会让配置、政策与规模化决策变得更容易或更困难，因此重要的是了解那些大的架构差异——主要是集中式与去中心化之间的选择。

原书第 359 页

Centralized VCS · 集中式 VCS

In centralized VCS implementations, the model is one of a single central repository (likely stored on some shared compute resource for your organization). Although a developer can have files checked out and accessible on their local workstation, operations that interact on the version control status of those files need to be communicated to the central server (adding files, syncing, updating existing files, etc.). Any code that is committed by a developer is committed into that central repository. The first VCS implementations were all centralized VCSs.

在集中式 VCS 的实现中，其模型是单一中央仓库（很可能存储在你组织的某个共享计算资源上）。尽管开发者可以在本地工作站检出文件、并访问它们，但凡是与这些文件的版本控制状态交互的操作（添加文件、同步、更新既有文件等），都需要与中央服务器通信。开发者提交的任何代码，都提交到那个中央仓库里。最早的一批 VCS 实现都是集中式 VCS。

Going back to the 1970s and early 1980s, we see that the earliest of these VCSs, such as RCS, focused on locking and preventing multiple simultaneous edits. You could copy the contents of a repository, but if you wanted to edit a file, you might need to acquire a lock, enforced by the VCS, to ensure that only you are making edits. When you have completed an edit, you release the lock. The model worked fine when any given change was a quick thing, or if there was rarely more than one person that wanted the lock for a file at any given time. Small edits like tweaking config files worked OK, as did working on a small team that either kept disjointed working hours or that rarely worked on overlapping files for extended periods. This sort of simplistic locking has inherent problems with scale: it can work fine for a few people, but has the potential to fall apart with larger groups if any of those locks become contended.

回到 1970 年代和 80 年代初，我们看到这些 VCS 中最早的一批（如 RCS）聚焦于锁定、防止多人同时编辑。你可以复制一个仓库的内容，但如果你想编辑一个文件，可能需要获取一把由 VCS 强制实施的锁，以确保只有你在做编辑。完成编辑后，你释放这把锁。当任何一次变更都很快、或任一时刻很少有超过一个人想要某个文件的锁时，这个模型运转良好。调整配置文件这类小改动没问题；在一个小团队里工作也没问题——要么大家工作时间不重叠，要么很少会长时间在重叠文件上工作。这种简单的锁定在规模上有固有问题：对几个人可以运转良好，但如果这些锁中任何一把出现争用，在更大的群体中就有可能崩解。

As a response to this scaling problem, the VCSs that were popular through the 90s and early 2000s operated at a higher level. These more modern centralized VCSs avoid the exclusive locking but track which changes you have synced, requiring your edit to be based on the most-current version of every file in your commit. CVS wrapped and refined RCS by (mostly) operating on batches of files at a time and allowing multiple developers to check out a file at the same time: so long as your base version contained all of the changes in the repository, you are allowed to commit. Subversion advanced further by providing true atomicity for commits, version tracking, and better tracking for unusual operations (renames, use of symbolic links, etc.). The centralized repository/checked-out client model continues today within Subversion as well as most commercial VCSs.

为应对这一规模化问题，在 90 年代和 2000 年代初流行的 VCS 在更高层面上运作。这些更现代的集中式 VCS 避免了排他锁，但会跟踪你已同步了哪些变更，要求你的编辑基于你提交中每个文件的最新版本。CVS 对 RCS 做了包装与改进：（大体上）一次对一批文件操作，并允许多名开发者同时检出一个文件——只要你的基础版本包含了仓库中的全部变更，你就被允许提交。Subversion 更进一步，为提交提供了真正的原子性、版本跟踪，以及对非常规操作（重命名、符号链接的使用等）更好的跟踪。中央仓库/检出客户端这一模型，在今天的 Subversion 以及大多数商业 VCS 中仍在沿用。

Distributed VCS · 分布式 VCS

Starting in the mid-2000s, many popular VCSs followed the Distributed Version Control System (DVCS) paradigm, seen in systems like Git and Mercurial. The

从 2000 年代中期开始，许多流行的 VCS 遵循分布式版本控制系统（DVCS）范式，如 Git 和 Mercurial 等系统所示。

原书第 360 页

primary conceptual difference between DVCS and more traditional centralized VCS (Subversion, CVS) is the question: Where can you commit? or perhaps, Which copies of these files count as a repository?

DVCS 与更传统的集中式 VCS（Subversion、CVS）之间的主要概念差异，在于这样一个问题：你能在哪里提交？或者说，这些文件的哪些副本才算作一个仓库？

A DVCS world does not enforce the constraint of a central repository: if you have a copy (clone, fork) of the repository, you have a repository that you can commit to as well as all of the metadata necessary to query for information about things like revision history. A standard workflow is to clone some existing repository, make some edits, commit them locally, and then push some set of commits to another repository, which may or may not be the original source of the clone. Any notion of centrality is purely conceptual, a matter of policy, not fundamental to the technology or the underlying protocols.

DVCS 的世界并不强制“中央仓库”这一约束：如果你拥有该仓库的一份副本（clone、fork），你就拥有了一个可以提交的仓库，以及查询修订历史等信息所需的全部元数据。一个标准工作流是：克隆某个既有仓库，做一些编辑，在本地提交，然后把某一组提交推送到另一个仓库——那个仓库可能是、也可能不是当初克隆的来源。任何“中央性”的概念都纯粹是概念上的、是政策问题，而非技术或底层协议所固有的。

The DVCS model allows for better offline operation and collaboration without inherently declaring one particular repository to be the source of truth. One repository is not necessarily ahead or behind because changes are not inherently projected into a linear timeline. However, considering common usage, both the centralized and DVCS models are largely interchangeable: whereas a centralized VCS provides a clearly defined central repository through technology, most DVCS ecosystems define a central repository for a project as a matter of policy. That is, most DVCS projects are built around one conceptual source of truth (a particular repository on GitHub, for instance). DVCS models tend to assume a more distributed use case and have found particularly strong adoption in the open source world.

DVCS 模型允许更好的离线操作与协作，而不必固有地宣告某个特定仓库为真相之源。一个仓库并不必然“领先”或“落后”，因为变更并不固有地被投射到一条线性时间线上。然而，考虑到常见用法，集中式与 DVCS 两种模型在很大程度上是可互换的：集中式 VCS 通过技术提供一个明确定义的中央仓库，而大多数 DVCS 生态则以政策形式为项目定义一个中央仓库。也就是说，大多数 DVCS 项目都围绕一个概念上的真相之源构建（例如 GitHub 上的某个特定仓库）。DVCS 模型倾向于假设一种更分布式的用例，并在开源世界中获得了尤其强劲的采用。

Generally speaking, the dominant source control system today is Git, which implements DVCS. When in doubt, use that—there is some value in doing what everyone else does. If your use cases are expected to be unusual, gather some data and evaluate the trade-offs.

总体而言，当今占主导地位的源代码管理系统是 Git，它实现了 DVCS。拿不准时就用它——随大流做事情有一定价值。如果你的用例预计会不同寻常，那就收集一些数据、评估一下各种权衡。

Google has a complex relationship with DVCS: our main repository is based on a (massive) custom in-house centralized VCS. There are periodic attempts to integrate more standard external options and to match the workflow that our engineers (especially Nooglers) have come to expect from external development. Unfortunately, those attempts to move toward more common tools like Git have been stymied by the sheer size of the codebase and userbase, to say nothing of Hyrum's Law effects tying us to a particular VCS and interface for that VCS. This is perhaps not surprising: most existing tools do not scale well with 50,000 engineers and tens of millions of

Google 与 DVCS 的关系很复杂：我们的主仓库基于一个（体量巨大的）自研集中式 VCS。我们周期性地尝试集成更标准的外部选项，并匹配我们工程师（尤其是 Noogler）从外部开发中所习惯的工作流。遗憾的是，那些转向 Git 等更常见工具的尝试，被代码库与用户群的庞大规模所阻碍，更不用说 Hyrum 定律效应把我们绑定到了某个特定 VCS 及其接口上。这或许并不令人意外：大多数现有工具，并不能很好地扩展到 5 万名工程师、数千万

原书第 361 页

commits. The DVCS model, which often (but not always) includes transmission of history and metadata, requires a lot of data to spin up a repository to work out of. In our workflow, centrality and in-the-cloud storage for the codebase seem to be critical to scaling. The DVCS model is built around the idea of downloading the entire codebase and having access to it locally. In practice, over time and as your organization scales up, any given developer is going to operate on a relatively smaller percentage of the files in a repository, and a small fraction of the versions of those files. As we grow (in file count and engineer count), that transmission becomes almost entirely waste. The only need for locality for most files occurs when building, but distributed (and reproducible) build systems seem to scale better for that task as well (see Chapter 18).

次提交的规模。DVCS 模型通常（但并非总是）包含历史与元数据的传输，它需要大量数据才能拉起一个可供工作的仓库。在我们的工作流中，中央性以及代码库在云端的存储，对规模化似乎至关重要。DVCS 模型是围绕“下载整个代码库、在本地访问它”这一想法构建的。实践中，随着时间推移、组织扩大，任一开发者所操作的文件，只占仓库中文件总数相对较小的比例，所操作的版本也只是这些文件版本中的一小部分。随着我们（在文件数与工程师数上）增长，那种传输几乎完全成了浪费。对大多数文件而言，唯一需要本地副本的时候是构建时；而分布式（且可复现）的构建系统在那项任务上似乎同样能更好地扩展（见第 18 章）。

Source of Truth · 真相之源

Centralized VCSs (Subversion, CVS, Perforce, etc.) bake the source-of-truth notion into the very design of the system: whatever is most recently committed at trunk is the current version. When a developer goes to check out the project, by default that trunk version is what they will be presented with. Your changes are done when they have been recommitted on top of that version.

集中式 VCS（Subversion、CVS、Perforce 等）把“真相之源”的概念直接烘焙进了系统设计之中：在主干上最近提交的内容，就是当前版本。当开发者去检出项目时，默认呈现给他们的就是那个主干版本。当你的变更被重新提交到那个版本之上时，它们才算“完成”。

However, unlike centralized VCS, there is no inherent notion of which copy of the distributed repository is the single source of truth in DVCS systems. In theory, it is possible to pass around commit tags and PRs with no centralization or coordination, allowing disparate branches of development to propagate unchecked, and thus risking a conceptual return to the world of Presentation v5 - final - redlines - Josh's version v2. Because of this, DVCS requires more explicit policy and norms than a centralized VCS does.

然而，与集中式 VCS 不同，在 DVCS 系统中，并不存在“分布式仓库的哪一份副本是唯一真相之源”这一固有概念。理论上，可以在没有中央化或协调的情况下到处传递提交标签与 PR，让各不相同的开发分支不受检查地传播，从而在概念上有退回到“Presentation v5 - final - redlines - Josh's version v2”那个世界的风险。正因如此，DVCS 比集中式 VCS 需要更显式的政策与规范。

Well-managed projects using DVCS declare one specific branch in one specific repository to be the source of truth and thus avoid the more chaotic possibilities. We see this in practice with the spread of hosted DVCS solutions like GitHub or GitLab—users can clone and fork the repository for a project, but there is still a single primary repository: things are done when they are in the trunk branch on that repository. It is not an accident that centralization and Source of Truth has crept back into the usage even in a DVCS world. To help illustrate just how important this Source of Truth idea is, let us imagine what happens when we do not have a clear source of truth.

使用 DVCS 且管理良好的项目，会声明某个特定仓库中的某个特定分支为真相之源，从而避免更混乱的可能性。我们在实践中看到这一点：随着 GitHub 或 GitLab 等托管式 DVCS 方案的普及——用户可以克隆、fork 一个项目的仓库，但仍然存在一个唯一的主仓库：当东西进入该仓库的主干分支时，就算“完成”了。即便在 DVCS 的世界里，中央化与“真相之源”也悄悄回到了用法之中，这并非偶然。为了说明“真相之源”这个概念究竟有多重要，让我们想象一下：当我们没有一个清晰的真相之源时，会发生什么。

原书第 362 页

Scenario: no clear source of truth · 场景：没有清晰的真相之源

Imagine that your team adheres to the DVCS philosophy enough to avoid defining a specific branch+repository as the ultimate source of truth.

想象一下：你的团队足够信奉 DVCS 哲学，以至于不去定义一个特定的“分支+仓库”作为最终真相之源。

In some respects, this is reminiscent of the Presentation v5 - final - redlines - Josh's version v2 model—after you pull from a teammate's repository, it is not necessarily clear which changes are present and which are not. In some respects, it is better than that because the DVCS model tracks the merging of individual patches at a much finer granularity than those ad hoc naming schemes, but there is a difference between the DVCS knowing which changes are incorporated and every engineer being sure they have all the past/relevant changes represented.

在某些方面，这让人想起“Presentation v5 - final - redlines - Josh's version v2”那个模型——当你从 teammate 的仓库拉取之后，并不一定清楚哪些变更已包含、哪些没有。在某些方面它比那个模型好，因为 DVCS 模型以比那些临时命名方案细得多的粒度跟踪单个补丁的合并；但“DVCS 知道哪些变更已并入”与“每位工程师确信自己已具备所有过往/相关变更”之间，是有差别的。

Consider what it takes to ensure that a release build includes all of the features that have been developed by each developer for the past few weeks. What (noncentralized, scalable) mechanisms are there to do that? Can we design policies that are fundamentally better than having everyone sign off? Are there any that require only sublinear human effort as the team scales up? Is that going to continue working as the number of developers on the team scales up? As far as we can see: probably not. Without a central Source of Truth, someone is going to keep a list of which features are potentially ready to be included in the next release. Eventually that bookkeeping is reproducing the model of having a centralized Source of Truth.

想一想：要确保一次发布构建包含了每位开发者在过去几周里开发的全部功能，需要做什么？有哪些（非中央化的、可扩展的）机制能做到这一点？我们能否设计出从根本上优于“让所有人签字确认”的政策？有没有哪种政策，在团队扩大时只需要次线性的人力投入？当团队中开发者数量增长时，它还能继续奏效吗？就我们所见：大概不能。没有中央的真相之源，就会有人去维护一份清单，记录哪些功能可能已准备好纳入下一次发布。最终，这种记账活动就重现了“拥有一个中央真相之源”的模型。

Further imagine: when a new developer joins the team, where do they get a fresh, known-good copy of the code?

再想象一下：当一名新开发者加入团队时，他从哪里获得一份新鲜的、已知良好的代码副本？

DVCS enables a lot of great workflows and interesting usage models. But if you are concerned with finding a system that requires sublinear human effort to manage as the team grows, it is pretty important to have one repository (and one branch) actually defined to be the ultimate source of truth.

DVCS 催生了许多很棒的工作流与有趣的使用模型。但如果你关心的是：找到一个在团队扩大时只需次线性人力投入来管理的系统，那么实际定义一个仓库（和一个分支）为最终真相之源，就相当重要。

There is some relativity in that Source of Truth. That is, for a given project, that Source of Truth might be different for a different organization. This caveat is important: it is reasonable for engineers at Google or RedHat to have different Sources of Truth for Linux Kernel patches, still different than Linus (the Linux Kernel maintainer) himself would. DVCS works fine when organizations and their Sources of Truth are hierarchical (and invisible to those outside the organization)—that is perhaps the most practically useful effect of the DVCS model. A RedHat engineer can commit to the local Source of Truth repository, and changes can be pushed from there upstream periodically, while Linus has a completely different notion of what is the Source of Truth. So long as there is no choice or uncertainty as to where a change should be pushed, we can avoid a large class of chaotic scaling problems in the DVCS model.

那个真相之源存在一定的相对性。也就是说，对一个给定项目，不同组织的真相之源可能不同。这个限定很重要：Google 或 RedHat 的工程师对 Linux 内核补丁拥有不同的真相之源，而这又不同于 Linus（Linux 内核维护者）本人所认定的真相之源——这是合理的。当组织及其真相之源是分层的（且对组织外部不可见）时，DVCS 运转良好——这或许是 DVCS 模型在实践中最有用的效果。RedHat 的工程师可以提交到本地的真相之源仓库，变更可以定期从那里向上游推送，而 Linus 对何为真相之源有完全不同的概念。只要“一个变更应当推送到哪里”不存在选择或不确定性，我们就能在 DVCS 模型中避免一大类混乱的规模化问题。

In all of this thinking, we are assigning special significance to the trunk branch. But of course, trunk in your VCS is only the technology default, and an organization can

在所有这些思考中，我们都在赋予主干分支特殊的重要性。但当然，你 VCS 中的“主干”只是技术上的默认值，一个组织可以

原书第 363 页

choose different policies on top of that. Perhaps the default branch has been abandoned and all work actually happens on some custom development branch—other than needing to provide a branch name in more operations, there is nothing inherently broken in that approach; it is just nonstandard. There is an (oft-unspoken) truth when discussing version control: the technology is only one part of it for any given organization; there is almost always an equal amount of policy and usage convention on top of that.

在此之上选择不同的政策。也许默认分支已被废弃、所有工作实际都发生在某个自定义开发分支上——除了需要在更多操作中提供分支名之外，这种做法本身并没有什么问题；它只是不合常规而已。在讨论版本控制时，有一个（常常未言明的）真相：对任何给定组织而言，技术只是其中一部分；在此之上，几乎总还有同等分量的政策与使用惯例。

No topic in version control has more policy and convention than the discussion of how to use and manage branches. We look at branch management in more detail in the next section.

在版本控制中，没有哪个话题比“如何使用与管理分支”的讨论包含更多政策与惯例。我们将在下一节更详细地考察分支管理。

Version Control Versus Dependency Management · 版本控制与依赖管理

There is a lot of conceptual similarity between discussions of version control policies and dependency management (see Chapter 21). The differences are primarily in two forms: VCS policies are largely about how you manage your own code, and are usually much finer grained. Dependency management is more challenging because we primarily focus on projects managed and controlled by other organizations, at a higher granularity, and these situations mean that you do not have perfect control. We will discuss a lot more of these high-level issues later in the book.

版本控制政策的讨论与依赖管理（见第 21 章）之间有大量概念上的相似之处。差异主要体现在两个方面：VCS 政策大体上是关于你如何管理自己的代码，且通常粒度细得多。依赖管理更具挑战，因为我们主要关注由其他组织管理与控制的项目、且粒度更高，而这些情形意味着你并不拥有完全的控制权。我们将在本书后面更多地讨论这些高层问题。

Branch Management · 分支管理

Being able to track different revisions in version control opens up a variety of different approaches for how to manage those different versions. Collectively, these different approaches fall under the term branch management, in contrast to a single trunk.

能够在版本控制中跟踪不同修订，为“如何管理这些不同版本”开辟了多种不同做法。这些不同做法统称为分支管理，以区别于单一主干。

Work in Progress Is Akin to a Branch · 在制品类似于一个分支

Any discussion that an organization has about branch management policies ought to at least acknowledge that every piece of work-in-progress in the organization is equivalent to a branch. This is more explicitly the case with a DVCS in which developers are more likely to make numerous local staging commits before pushing back to the upstream Source of Truth. This is still true of centralized VCSs: uncommitted local changes are not conceptually different than committed changes on a branch, other than potentially being more difficult to find and diff against. Some centralized systems even make this explicit. For example, when using Perforce, every change is given two revision numbers: one indicating the implicit branch point where the change was created, and one indicating where it was recommitted, as illustrated in Figure 16-1. Perforce users can query to see who has outstanding changes to a given file, inspect the pending changes in other users' uncommitted changes, and more.

一个组织关于分支管理政策的任何讨论，至少应当承认：组织中每一件在制品（work-in-progress）都等价于一个分支。在 DVCS 中，这一点更为显式——开发者在推回上游真相之源之前，更可能做出大量本地暂存提交。这对集中式 VCS 同样成立：未提交的本地变更，与“在某个分支上已提交的变更”在概念上并无不同，除了前者可能更难查找、更难做 diff 之外。有些集中式系统甚至把这一点显式化。例如，使用 Perforce 时，每次变更都会被赋予两个版本号：一个指示该变更被创建时那个隐式分支点，另一个指示它被重新提交到的位置，如图 16-1 所示。Perforce 用户可以查询谁对某个给定文件有未决变更、查看其他用户未提交变更中的待处理变更等等。

原书第 364 页

This uncommitted work is akin to a branch idea is particularly relevant when thinking about refactoring tasks. Imagine a developer being told, Go rename Widget to OldWidget. Depending on an organization's branch management policies and understanding, what counts as a branch, and which branches matter, this could have several interpretations:

这种“未提交的工作类似于一个分支”的想法，在思考重构任务时尤其相关。想象一名开发者被告知：“去把 Widget 改名为 OldWidget。”根据一个组织的分支管理政策与理解、以及“什么算一个分支、哪些分支重要”，这可能有好几种解释：

  • Rename Widget on the trunk branch in the Source of Truth repository

    在真相之源仓库的主干分支上把 Widget 改名

  • Rename Widget on all branches in the Source of Truth repository

    在真相之源仓库的所有分支上把 Widget 改名

  • Rename Widget on all branches in the Source of Truth repository, and find all devs with outstanding changes to files that reference Widget

    在真相之源仓库的所有分支上把 Widget 改名，并找出所有对引用了 Widget 的文件有未决变更的开发者

If we were to speculate, attempting to support that rename this everywhere, even in outstanding changes use case is part of why commercial centralized VCSs tend to track things like which engineers have this file open for editing? (We do not think this is a scalable way to perform a refactoring task, but we understand the point of view.)

如果让我们推测一下：试图支持那种“在所有地方都改名，包括未决变更中”的用例，正是商业集中式 VCS 倾向于跟踪“哪些工程师把这个文件打开着编辑”之类信息的部分原因。（我们不认为这是一种可扩展的执行重构任务的方式，但我们理解这种观点。）

Dev Branches · 开发分支

In the age before consistent unit testing (see Chapter 11), when the introduction of any given change had a high risk of regressing functionality elsewhere in the system, it made sense to treat trunk specially. We do not commit to trunk, your Tech Lead might say, until new changes have gone through a full round of testing. Our team uses feature-specific development branches instead.

在一致的单元测试（见第 11 章）普及之前的年代，引入任何一次变更都有很高的风险在系统别处造成功能回归，那时对主干采取特殊对待是有道理的。“我们不直接提交到主干，”你的技术负责人可能会说，“要等新变更经过一整轮测试之后。我们团队改用按功能划分的开发分支。”

A development branch (usually dev branch) is a halfway point between this is done but not committed and this is what new work is based on. The problem that these are attempting to solve (instability of the product) is a legitimate one—but one that

一个开发分支（通常简称 dev 分支）是介于“这已完成但未提交”与“这是新工作所基于的东西”之间的一个中途点。它们试图解决的问题（产品的不稳定性）是一个正当问题——但我们

原书第 365 页

we have found to be solved far better with more extensive use of tests, Continuous Integration (CI) (see Chapter 23), and quality enforcement practices like thorough code review.

发现：通过更广泛地使用测试、持续集成（CI，见第 23 章）以及彻底的代码评审等质量强制实践，能远为更好地解决它。

We believe that a version control policy that makes extensive use of dev branches as a means toward product stability is inherently misguided. The same set of commits are going to be merged to trunk eventually. Small merges are easier than big ones. Merges done by the engineer who authored those changes are easier than batching unrelated changes and merging later (which will happen eventually if a team is sharing a dev branch). If presubmit testing on the merge reveals any new problems, the same argument applies: it is easier to determine whose changes are responsible for a regression if there is only one engineer involved. Merging a large dev branch implies that more changes are happening in that test run, making failures more difficult to isolate. Triaging and root-causing the problem is difficult; fixing it is even worse.

我们认为：把大量使用开发分支作为实现产品稳定性手段的版本控制政策，从根本上就是被误导的。同一组提交最终总要合并到主干。小合并比大合并容易。由编写这些变更的工程师本人来做合并，比把不相关的变更攒成一批、稍后再合并要容易（如果一个团队共享一个 dev 分支，后者最终必然发生）。如果对合并的提交前测试暴露出任何新问题，同样的论点也适用：如果只涉及一名工程师，更容易确定是谁的变更导致了回归。合并一个大型 dev 分支意味着那次测试运行中发生了更多变更，使失败更难隔离。对问题做分流、定位根因都很困难；修复它就更糟了。

Beyond the lack of expertise and inherent problems in merging a single branch, there are significant scaling risks when relying on dev branches. This is a very common productivity drain for a software organization. When there are multiple branches being developed in isolation for long periods, coordinating merge operations becomes significantly more expensive (and possibly riskier) than they would be with trunk-based development.

除了合并单个分支所缺乏的专业能力与固有问题之外，依赖 dev 分支还存在显著的规模化风险。这对软件组织而言是一种非常常见的生产力消耗。当有多个分支长期在隔离状态下开发时，协调合并操作的成本，会比基于主干的开发高得多（也可能风险更大）。

How did we become addicted to dev branches? · 我们是如何对 dev 分支上瘾的？

It is easy to see how organizations fall into this trap: they see, Merging this long-lived development branch reduced stability and conclude, Branch merges are risky. Rather than solve that with Better testing and Do not use branch-based development strategies, they focus on slowing down and coordinating the symptom: the branch merges. Teams begin developing new branches based on other in-flight branches. Teams working on a long-lived dev branch might or might not regularly have that branch synched with the main development branch. As the organization scales up, the number of development branches grows as well, and the more effort is placed on coordinating that branch merge strategy. Increasing effort is thrown at coordination of branch merges—a task that inherently does not scale. Some unlucky engineer becomes the Build Master/Merge Coordinator/Content Management Engineer, focused on acting as the single point coordinator to merge all the disparate branches in the organization. Regularly scheduled meetings attempt to ensure that the organization has worked out the merge strategy for the week. The teams that are not chosen to merge often need to re-sync and retest after each of these large merges.

很容易看出组织是如何掉进这个陷阱的：他们看到“合并这个长期 dev 分支降低了稳定性”，于是得出结论“分支合并是有风险的”。他们不去用“更好的测试”和“不要使用基于分支的开发策略”来解决问题，而是把精力放在放慢并协调那个症状上：分支合并。团队开始基于其他在途分支开发新分支。在一个长期 dev 分支上工作的团队，可能会、也可能不会定期把该分支与主开发分支同步。随着组织扩大，开发分支的数量也增长，花在协调那套分支合并策略上的精力也越多。越来越多的精力被投入到分支合并的协调上——而这是一项本质上不可扩展的任务。某个不幸的工程师成了构建主管/合并协调员/内容管理工程师，专注于作为单点协调员，把组织中所有各不相同的分支合并起来。定期召开的会议试图确保组织已经“制定好本周的合并策略”。那些没被选中做合并的团队，往往在每次这种大合并之后都需要重新同步、重新测试。

原书第 366 页

All of that effort in merging and retesting is pure overhead. The alternative requires a different paradigm: trunk-based development, rely heavily on testing and CI, keep the build green, and disable incomplete/untested features at runtime. Everyone is responsible to sync to trunk and commit; no merge strategy meetings, no large/expensive merges. And, no heated discussions about which version of a library should be used—there can be only one. There must be a single Source of Truth. In the end, there will be a single revision used for a release: narrowing down to a single source of truth is just the shift left approach for identifying what is and is not being included.

所有这些在合并与重新测试上的精力，都是纯粹的开销。替代方案需要一种不同的范式：基于主干的开发，重度依赖测试与 CI，保持构建常绿，并在运行时禁用未完成/未测试的功能。每个人都有责任同步到主干并提交；没有“合并策略”会议，没有大型/昂贵的合并。而且，也不再有关于“该使用哪个版本的库”的激烈讨论——只能有一个版本。必须有唯一的真相之源。最终，一次发布总会使用某个唯一的修订版本：收窄到唯一的真相之源，不过就是“左移”地识别哪些东西被纳入、哪些没有。

Release Branches · 发布分支

If the period between releases (or the release lifetime) for a product is longer than a few hours, it may be sensible to create a release branch that represents the exact code that went into the release build for your product. If any critical flaws are discovered between the actual release of that product into the wild and the next release cycle, fixes can be cherry-picked (a minimal, targeted merge) from trunk to your release branch.

如果一个产品两次发布之间的间隔（或发布的生命周期）长于几个小时，那么创建一个发布分支、代表进入该产品发布构建的确切代码，可能是合理的。如果在该产品实际发布到外界之后、到下一个发布周期之间发现任何关键缺陷，可以从主干把修复 cherry-pick（最小化、有针对性的合并）到你的发布分支。

By comparison to dev branches, release branches are generally benign: it is not the technology of branches that is troublesome, it is the usage. The primary difference between a dev branch and a release branch is the expected end state: a dev branch is expected to merge back to trunk, and could even be further branched by another team. A release branch is expected to be abandoned eventually.

与 dev 分支相比，发布分支总体上是良性的：麻烦的不是分支这项技术，而是它的用法。dev 分支与发布分支的主要差异在于预期的终态：dev 分支预期要合并回主干，甚至可能被另一个团队进一步分出分支；而发布分支预期最终会被废弃。

In the highest-functioning technical organizations that Google's DevOps Research and Assessment (DORA) organization has identified, release branches are practically nonexistent. Organizations that have achieved Continuous Deployment (CD)—the ability to release from trunk many times a day—likely tend to skip release branches: it is much easier to simply add the fix and redeploy. Thus, cherry-picks and branches seem like unnecessary overhead. Obviously, this is more applicable to organizations that deploy digitally (such as web services and apps) than those that push any form of tangible release to customers; it is generally valuable to know exactly what has been pushed to customers.

在 Google 的 DevOps 研究与评估（DORA）组织所识别出的最高效能技术组织中，发布分支几乎不存在。那些已实现持续部署（CD）——即每天可从主干发布多次——的组织，往往倾向于跳过发布分支：直接加上修复再重新部署要容易得多。因此，cherry-pick 和分支看似不必要的开销。显然，这更适用于以数字方式部署的组织（如 Web 服务和应用），而不是那些向客户推送任何形式有形发布的组织；确切知道向客户推送了什么，通常是有价值的。

That same DORA research also suggests a strong positive correlation between trunk-based development, no long-lived dev branches, and good technical outcomes. The underlying idea in both of those ideas seems clear: branches are a drag on productivity. In many cases we think complex branch and merge strategies are a perceived safety crutch—an attempt to keep trunk stable. As we see throughout this book, there are other ways to achieve that outcome.

同一项 DORA 研究还表明：“基于主干的开发”“不使用长期 dev 分支”与良好的技术成果之间存在强正相关。这两个想法背后的基本道理很清楚：分支是生产力的拖累。在许多情况下，我们认为复杂的分支与合并策略是一种被感知到的安全拐杖——试图借此保持主干稳定。正如我们在本书各处所见，要达到那个目标还有其他办法。

原书第 367 页

Version Control at Google · Google 的版本控制

At Google, the vast majority of our source is managed in a single repository (monorepo) shared among roughly 50,000 engineers. Almost all projects that are owned by Google live there, except large open source projects like Chromium and Android. This includes public-facing products like Search, Gmail, our advertising products, our Google Cloud Platform offerings, as well as the internal infrastructure necessary to support and develop all of those products.

在 Google，我们的绝大部分源代码都管理在一个单一仓库（monorepo）中，约 5 万名工程师共享。除了 Chromium、Android 这样的大型开源项目外，几乎所有由 Google 拥有的项目都在那里。这包括面向公众的产品（如搜索、Gmail、我们的广告产品、Google Cloud Platform 各产品），以及支持与开发所有这些产品所需的内部基础设施。

We rely on an in-house-developed centralized VCS called Piper, built to run as a distributed microservice in our production environment. This has allowed us to use Google-standard storage, communication, and Compute as a Service technology to provide a globally available VCS storing more than 80 TB of content and metadata. The Piper monorepo is then simultaneously edited and committed to by many thousands of engineers every day. Between humans and semiautomated processes that make use of version control (or improve things checked into VCS), we will regularly handle 60,000 to 70,000 commits to the repository per work day. Binary artifacts are fairly common because the full repository is not transmitted and thus the normal costs of binary artifacts do not really apply. Because of the focus on Google-scale from the earliest conception, operations in this VCS ecosystem are still cheap at human scale: it takes perhaps 15 seconds total to create a new client at trunk, add a file, and commit an (unreviewed) change to Piper. This low-latency interaction and well-understood/well-designed scaling simplifies a lot of the developer experience.

我们依赖一个名为 Piper 的自研集中式 VCS，它被构建为在生产环境中以分布式微服务形式运行。这让我们能够使用 Google 标准的存储、通信以及“计算即服务”技术，提供一个全球可用、存储超过 80 TB 内容与元数据的 VCS。Piper 单体仓库每天有数以千计的工程师同时编辑并提交。在利用版本控制（或改进提交到 VCS 的内容）的人与半自动化流程之间，我们每个工作日通常要处理 6 万到 7 万次提交。二进制制品相当常见，因为整个仓库不会被传输，所以二进制制品的常规成本在此并不真正适用。由于从最早构想起就聚焦于 Google 规模，这个 VCS 生态中的操作在人类规模下仍然廉价：在主干上创建一个新客户端、添加一个文件、并向 Piper 提交一个（未经评审的）变更，总共大约只需 15 秒。这种低延迟交互以及被充分理解、设计良好的规模化，简化了大量开发者体验。

By virtue of Piper being an in-house product, we have the ability to customize it and enforce whatever source control policies we choose. For instance, we have a notion of granular ownership in the monorepo: at every level of the file hierarchy, we can find OWNERS files that list the usernames of engineers that are allowed to approve commits within that subtree of the repository (in addition to the OWNERS that are listed at higher levels in the tree). In an environment with many repositories, this might have been achieved by having separate repositories with filesystem permissions enforcement controlling commit access or via a Git commit hook (action triggered at commit time) to do a separate permissions check. By controlling the VCS, we can make the concept of ownership and approval more explicit and enforced by the VCS during an attempted commit operation. The model is also flexible: ownership is just a text file, not tied to a physical separation of repositories, so it is trivial to update as the result of a team transfer or organization restructuring.

由于 Piper 是自研产品，我们有能力定制它、并强制执行我们选择的任何源代码管理政策。例如，我们在单体仓库中有一个细粒度所有权的概念：在文件层级的每一层，都能找到 OWNERS 文件，列出被允许批准该仓库子树内提交的工程师用户名（除了树中更高层所列的 OWNERS 之外）。在一个拥有众多仓库的环境中，这可能要通过带文件系统权限强制、控制提交访问的独立仓库来实现，或通过 Git 提交钩子（提交时触发的动作）来做一次独立的权限检查。通过控制 VCS，我们可以让“所有权与批准”这一概念更显式，并在尝试提交操作时由 VCS 强制实施。这个模型还很灵活：所有权只是一个文本文件，不与仓库的物理分离绑定，因此在团队调动或组织重组时更新它易如反掌。

One Version · 单一版本

The incredible scaling powers of Piper alone would not allow the sort of collaboration that we rely upon. As we said earlier: version control is also about policy. In addition to our VCS, one key feature of Google's version control policy is what we have come to refer to as One Version. This extends the Single Source of Truth concept we

单凭 Piper 令人惊叹的扩展能力，并不足以支撑我们所依赖的那种协作。正如我们前面所说：版本控制也关乎政策。除了我们的 VCS 之外，Google 版本控制政策的一个关键特征，就是我们所称的“单一版本”（One Version）。它把我们先前看到的“唯一真相之源”概念

原书第 368 页

looked at earlier—ensuring that a developer knows which branch and repository is their source of truth—to something like For every dependency in our repository, there must be only one version of that dependency to choose. For third-party packages, this means that there can be only a single version of that package checked into our repository, in the steady state. For internal packages, this means no forking without repackaging/renaming: it must be technologically safe to mix both the original and the fork into the same project with no special effort. This is a powerful feature for our ecosystem: there are very few packages with restrictions like If you include this package (A), you cannot include other package (B).

——确保开发者知道哪个分支、哪个仓库是他们的真相之源——扩展为这样一条规则：“对我们仓库中的每一个依赖，只能有一个版本可供选择。”对第三方包而言，这意味着：在稳态下，该包只能有一个版本被签入我们的仓库。对内部包而言，这意味着不重新打包/改名就不得 fork：必须能在无需特殊努力的情况下，把原版与 fork 版混用到同一个项目中，且在技术上是安全的。这对我们的生态是一项强大的特性：很少有包带有“如果你包含了这个包（A），就不能包含另一个包（B）”这样的限制。

This notion of having a single copy on a single branch in a single repository as our Source of Truth is intuitive but also has some subtle depth in application. Let us investigate a scenario in which we have a monorepo (and thus arguably have fulfilled the letter of the law on Single Source of Truth), but have allowed forks of our libraries to propagate on trunk.

“在单个仓库的单个分支上拥有一份副本作为我们的真相之源”这一概念很直观，但在应用中也有一些微妙的深度。让我们考察这样一个场景：我们有一个单体仓库（从而可以说已经在字面上满足了“唯一真相之源”），但我们允许库的 fork 在主干上传播。

Scenario: Multiple Available Versions · 场景：存在多个可用版本

Imagine the following scenario: some team discovers a bug in common infrastructure code (in our case, Abseil or Guava or the like). Rather than fix it in place, the team decides to fork that infrastructure and tweak it to work around the bug—without renaming the library or the symbols. It informs other teams near them, Hey, we have an improved version of Abseil checked in over here: check it out. A few other teams build libraries that themselves rely on this new fork.

想象以下场景：某个团队在公共基础设施代码中（在我们这里是 Abseil、Guava 之类）发现了一个 bug。该团队不去原地修复，而是决定 fork 那套基础设施、并对其做些微调以绕过这个 bug——却不重命名库或符号。它通知身边的其他团队：“嘿，我们在这里签入了一个改进版的 Abseil，来看看吧。”另外几个团队构建了自己也依赖这个新 fork 的库。

As we will see in Chapter 21, we are now in a dangerous situation. If any project in the codebase comes to depend on both the original and the forked versions of Abseil simultaneously, in the best case, the build fails. In the worst case, we will be subjected to difficult-to-understand runtime bugs stemming from linking in two mismatched versions of the same library. The fork has effectively added a coloring/partitioning property to the codebase: the transitive dependency set for any given target must include exactly one copy of this library. Any link added from the original flavor partition of the codebase to the new fork partition will likely break things. This means that in the end that something as simple as adding a new dependency becomes an operation that might require running all tests for the entire codebase, to ensure that we have not violated one of these partitioning requirements. That is expensive, unfortunate, and does not scale well.

正如我们将在第 21 章看到的，我们此刻正处于危险境地。如果代码库中任何项目同时依赖 Abseil 的原版与 fork 版，最好的情况是构建失败；最坏的情况，则是我们将遭遇因链接了同一库的两个不匹配版本而产生的、难以理解的运行时 bug。那个“fork”实际上给代码库增加了一种着色/分区属性：任何给定目标的传递依赖集，必须恰好包含该库的一份副本。从代码库“原版风味”分区到“新 fork”分区的任何链接，都很可能把东西弄坏。这意味着：最终，“添加一个新依赖”这样简单的事，会变成一个可能需要运行整个代码库全部测试的操作，以确保我们没有违反这些分区要求之一。这既昂贵、又不幸，而且可扩展性很差。

原书第 369 页

In some cases, we might be able to hack things together in a way to allow a resulting executable to function correctly. Java, for instance, has a relatively standard practice called shading, which tweaks the names of the internal dependencies of a library to hide those dependencies from the rest of the application. When dealing with functions, this is technically sound, even if it is theoretically a bit of a hack. When dealing with types that can be passed from one package to another, shading solutions work neither in theory nor in practice. As far as we know, any technological trickery that allows multiple isolated versions of a library to function in the same binary share this limitation: that approach will work for functions, but there is no good (efficient) solution to shading types—multiple versions for any library that provides a vocabulary type (or any higher-level construct) will fail. Shading and related approaches are patching over the underlying issue: multiple versions of the same dependency are needed. (We will discuss how to minimize that in general in Chapter 21.)

在某些情况下，我们或许能把东西 hack 到一起，让最终产物可正确运行。例如，Java 有一种相对标准的做法叫做 shading（遮蔽），它会调整一个库的内部依赖的名称，把这些依赖对应用程序的其余部分隐藏起来。在处理函数时，这在技术上是合理的，哪怕理论上有点 hack 味道。但在处理可从一个包传递到另一个包的类型时，shading 方案在理论和实践上都行不通。据我们所知，任何允许同一库的多个隔离版本在同一个二进制中运转的技术花招，都共享这一局限：那种做法对函数可行，但对“给类型做 shading”没有好的（高效的）解决方案——任何提供词汇类型（或任何更高层构造）的库，其多版本都将失败。shading 及相关做法只是在掩盖底层问题：同一依赖需要多个版本。（我们将在第 21 章讨论如何总体上把这一点降到最小。）

Any policy system that allows for multiple versions in the same codebase is allowing for the possibility of these costly incompatibilities. It is possible that you will get away with it for a while (we certainly have a number of small violations of this policy), but in general, any multiple-version situation has a very real possibility of leading to big problems.

任何允许同一代码库中存在多个版本的政策系统，都是在允许这些代价高昂的不兼容性出现的可能。你也许能侥幸维持一阵（我们自己当然也有不少对这一政策的小违反），但总体而言，任何多版本情形都有非常现实的可能导致大问题。

The One-Version Rule · 单一版本规则

With that example in mind, on top of the Single Source of Truth model, we can hopefully understand the depth of this seemingly simple rule for source control and branch management:

带着这个例子，在“唯一真相之源”模型之上，我们有望理解这条看似简单的源代码管理与分支管理规则的深度：

Developers must never have a choice of What version of this component should I depend upon?

开发者绝不应该面临“我该依赖这个组件的哪个版本？”这样的选择。

Colloquially, this becomes something like a One-Version Rule. In practice, One-Version is not hard and fast, but phrasing this around limiting the versions that can be chosen when adding a new dependency conveys a very powerful understanding.

通俗地说，这就成了类似“单一版本规则”的东西。实践中，“单一版本”并不是一条硬性铁律，但围绕“在添加新依赖时限制可选择的版本”来表述它，传达了一种非常有力的理解。

For an individual developer, lack of choice can seem like an arbitrary impediment. Yet we see again and again that for an organization, it is a critical component in efficient scaling. Consistency has a profound importance at all levels in an organization. From one perspective, this is a direct side effect of discussions about consistency and ensuring the ability to leverage consistent choke points.

对个体开发者而言，缺乏选择可能看起来像一种任意设置的障碍。然而我们一次又一次地看到：对一个组织而言，它是高效规模化的关键组成部分。一致性在组织的各个层面都具有深远的重要性。从一个角度看，这正是“关于一致性的讨论”以及“确保能够利用一致的扼流点”所带来的直接副作用。

原书第 370 页

(Nearly) No Long-Lived Branches · （几乎）不设长期分支

There are several deeper ideas and policies implicit in our One-Version Rule; foremost among them: development branches should be minimal, or at best be very short lived. This follows from a lot of published work over the past 20 years, from Agile processes to DORA research results on trunk-based development and even Phoenix Project lessons on reducing work-in-progress. When we include the idea of pending work as akin to a dev branch, this further reinforces that work should be done in small increments against trunk, committed regularly.

在我们的“单一版本规则”中隐含着若干更深层的想法与政策；其中首要的一条是：开发分支应当尽量少，或者至多非常短命。这与过去 20 年里大量已发表的工作一致，从敏捷流程，到 DORA 关于基于主干开发的研究结果，乃至《凤凰项目》中关于“减少在制品”的经验。当我们把“待处理工作”也视为类似于一个 dev 分支时，这进一步强化了如下做法：工作应当以针对主干的小增量完成、并定期提交。

As a counterexample: in a development community that depends heavily on long-lived development branches, it is not difficult to imagine opportunity for choice creeping back in.

作为反例：在一个重度依赖长期开发分支的开发社区中，不难想象选择的机会会悄悄卷土重来。

Imagine this scenario: some infrastructure team is working on a new Widget, better than the old one. Excitement grows. Other newly started projects ask, Can we depend on your new Widget? Obviously, this can be handled if you have invested in codebase visibility policies, but the deep problem happens when the new Widget is allowed but only exists in a parallel branch. Remember: new development must not have a choice when adding a dependency. That new Widget should be committed to trunk, disabled from the runtime until it is ready, and hidden from other developers by visibility if possible—or the two Widget options should be designed such that they can coexist, linked into the same programs.

想象这个场景：某个基础设施团队正在开发一个新的 Widget，比旧的更好。兴奋感不断增长。其他新启动的项目问：“我们能依赖你的新 Widget 吗？”显然，如果你已在代码库可见性政策上投入，这是可以处理的；但深层问题发生在：新 Widget 被“允许”了，却只存在于一个并行分支里。请记住：新开发在添加依赖时绝不能有选择。那个新 Widget 应当被提交到主干、在就绪前从运行时禁用，并在可能时通过可见性对其他开发者隐藏——或者，两个 Widget 选项应被设计成能够共存、链接进同一程序。

Interestingly, there is already evidence of this being important in the industry. In Accelerate and the most recent State of DevOps reports, DORA points out that there is a predictive relationship between trunk-based development and high-performing software organizations. Google is not the only organization to have discovered this—nor did we necessarily have expected outcomes in mind when these policies evolved—it just seemed like nothing else worked. DORA's result certainly matches our experience.

有趣的是，行业中已有证据表明这一点的重要性。在《Accelerate》以及最新的《DevOps 现状报告》中，DORA 指出：基于主干的开发与高绩效软件组织之间存在一种预测性关系。Google 并不是唯一发现这一点的组织——我们在这些政策演进时也未必心中有预期的结果——只是看起来别的办法都行不通。DORA 的结果当然与我们的经验吻合。

Our policies and tools for large-scale changes (LSCs; see Chapter 22) put additional weight on the importance of trunk-based development: broad/shallow changes that are applied across the codebase are already a massive (often tedious) undertaking when modifying everything checked in to the trunk branch. Having an unbounded number of additional dev branches that might need to be refactored at the same time would be an awfully large tax on executing those types of changes, finding an ever-expanding set of hidden branches. In a DVCS model, it might not even be possible to identify all of those branches.

我们用于大规模变更（LSC，见第 22 章）的政策与工具，进一步加重了“基于主干开发”的重要性：当修改签入主干分支的所有内容时，跨代码库施加的广泛/浅层次变更，本身就已经是一项庞大（往往枯燥）的工作。如果还有数量无界的额外 dev 分支可能需要同时被重构，那对执行那类变更将是一笔极其沉重的税——还得去找一套不断膨胀的隐藏分支。在 DVCS 模型中，甚至可能无法识别出所有这些分支。

原书第 371 页

Of course, our experience is not universal. You might find yourself in unusual situations that require longer-lived dev branches in parallel to (and regularly merged with) trunk.

当然，我们的经验并非放之四海而皆准。你可能会发现自己处于不同寻常的情形，需要与主干并行（并定期合并）的、存活更久的 dev 分支。

Those scenarios should be rare, and should be understood to be expensive. Across the roughly 1,000 teams that work in the Google monorepo, there are only a couple that have such a dev branch. Usually these exist for a very specific (and very unusual) reason. Most of those reasons boil down to some variation of We have an unusual requirement for compatibility over time. Oftentimes this is a matter of ensuring compatibility for data at rest across versions: readers and writers of some file format need to agree on that format over time even if the reader or writer implementations are modified. Other times, long-lived dev branches might come from promising API compatibility over time—when One Version is not enough and we need to promise that an older version of a microservice client still works with a newer server (or vice versa). That can be a very challenging requirement, something you should not promise lightly for an actively evolving API, and something you should treat carefully to ensure that period of time does not accidentally begin to grow. Dependency across time in any form is far more costly and complicated than code that is time invariant. Internally, Google production services make relatively few promises of that form. We also benefit greatly from a cap on potential version skew imposed by our build horizon: every job in production needs to be rebuilt and redeployed every six months, maximum. (Usually it is far more frequent than that.)

那些情形应当是罕见的，并且应被理解为代价高昂。在 Google 单体仓库中工作的约 1000 个团队里，只有两三个拥有这样的 dev 分支。通常这些分支出于非常具体（且非常不寻常）的原因而存在。这些原因大多可归结为某种变体：“我们对随时间的兼容性有不寻常的要求。”很多时候，这是要确保静态数据跨版本的兼容性：某种文件格式的读写双方，即使在读或写实现被修改后，也需要随时间在该格式上达成一致。另一些时候，长期 dev 分支可能来自对“随时间的 API 兼容性”的承诺——当“单一版本”还不够、而我们需要承诺一个微服务客户端的旧版本仍能与较新的服务器（或反之）协同工作时。那可能是一项极具挑战性的要求，对一个 actively 演进的 API 不应轻易承诺，也应当谨慎对待，以确保那段承诺时间不会意外地开始变长。任何形式的跨时间依赖，都远比时间不变的代码代价更高、更复杂。在内部，Google 生产服务做出的那种承诺相对较少。我们还极大地受益于“构建视野”（build horizon）对潜在版本偏移所施加的上限：生产中的每个作业最多每六个月就必须重新构建并重新部署一次。（通常远不止这个频率。）

We are sure there are other situations that might necessitate long-lived dev branches. Just make sure to keep them rare. If you adopt other tools and practices discussed in this book, many will tend to exert pressure against long-lived dev branches. Automation and tooling that works great at trunk and fails (or takes more effort) for a dev branch can help encourage developers to stay current.

我们确信还有其他可能需要长期 dev 分支的情形。只要确保它们保持罕见即可。如果你采用本书讨论的其他工具与实践，其中许多会倾向于对长期 dev 分支施加压力。那些在主干上运转良好、而在 dev 分支上失败（或需要更多努力）的自动化与工具，有助于鼓励开发者跟上最新状态。

What About Release Branches? · 那发布分支呢？

Many Google teams use release branches, with limited cherry picks. If you are going to put out a monthly release and continue working toward the next release, it is perfectly reasonable to make a release branch. Similarly, if you are going to ship devices to customers, it is valuable to know exactly what version is out in the field. Use caution and reason, keep cherry picks to a minimum, and do not plan to remerge with trunk. Our various teams have all sorts of policies about release branches given that relatively few teams have arrived at the sort of rapid release cadence promised by CD (see Chapter 24) that obviates the need or desire for a release branch. Generally speaking,

许多 Google 团队使用发布分支，并配合有限的 cherry-pick。如果你打算每月发布一次、并继续朝着下一次发布推进，那么做一个发布分支是完全合理的。同样，如果你要向客户交付设备，确切知道“现场”是什么版本是有价值的。请谨慎、理性，把 cherry-pick 降到最少，并且不要计划再合并回主干。我们各团队对发布分支有各种各样的政策，因为相对较少的团队达到了 CD（见第 24 章）所承诺的那种快速发布节奏——那种节奏会消除对发布分支的需要或渴望。总体而言，

原书第 372 页

release branches do not cause any widespread cost in our experience. Or, at least, no noticeable cost above and beyond the additional inherent cost to the VCS.

根据我们的经验，发布分支并不会造成任何广泛的成本。或者说，至少不会在 VCS 额外固有成本之上再造成可察觉的成本。

Monorepos · 单体仓库

In 2016, we published a (highly cited, much discussed) paper on Google's monorepo approach. The monorepo approach has some inherent benefits, and chief among them is that adhering to One Version is trivial: it is usually more difficult to violate One Version than it would be to do the right thing. There is no process of deciding which versions of anything are official, or discovering which repositories are important. Building tools to understand the state of the build (see Chapter 23) does not also require discovering where important repositories exist. Consistency helps scale up the impact of introducing new tools and optimizations. By and large, engineers can see what everyone else is doing and use that to inform their own choices in code and system design. These are all very good things.

2016 年，我们发表了一篇（被大量引用、被广泛讨论的）关于 Google 单体仓库做法的论文。单体仓库做法有一些固有好处，其中首要的是：遵守“单一版本”是轻而易举的——通常违反“单一版本”比做正确的事更难。不存在“决定哪些版本是官方版本”的流程，也不需要“发现哪些仓库重要”。构建用于理解构建状态的工具（见第 23 章），也不必同时去发现重要仓库位于何处。一致性有助于放大引入新工具与优化所带来的影响。大体上，工程师可以看到其他人都在做什么，并据此为自己在代码与系统设计中的选择提供参考。这些都是非常好的事。

Given all of that and our belief in the merits of the One-Version Rule, it is reasonable to ask whether a monorepo is the One True Way. By comparison, the open source community seems to work just fine with a manyrepo approach built on a seemingly infinite number of noncoordinating and nonsynchronized project repositories.

鉴于这一切，以及我们对“单一版本规则”优点的信念，人们有理由问：单体仓库是否就是唯一正道。相比之下，开源社区在一种“多仓库”做法下似乎运转良好——那是建立在看似无限多个互不协调、互不同步的项目仓库之上的。

In short: no, we do not think the monorepo approach as we have described it is the perfect answer for everyone. Continuing the parallel between filesystem format and VCS, it is easy to imagine deciding between using 10 drives to provide one very large logical filesystem or 10 smaller filesystems accessed separately. In a filesystem world, there are pros and cons to both. Technical issues when evaluating filesystem choice would range from outage resilience, size constraints, performance characteristics, and so on. Usability issues would likely focus more on the ability to reference files across filesystem boundaries, add symlinks, and synchronize files.

简而言之：不，我们并不认为我们所描述的单体仓库做法对每个人都是完美答案。继续把文件系统格式与 VCS 类比，很容易想象这样的抉择：是用 10 块磁盘提供一个非常大的逻辑文件系统，还是用 10 个较小的、分别访问的文件系统。在文件系统的世界里，两者各有利弊。评估文件系统选择时的技术问题，会涵盖故障恢复能力、容量限制、性能特征等等。可用性问题则更可能聚焦于跨文件系统边界引用文件、添加符号链接、同步文件的能力。

A very similar set of issues governs whether to prefer a monorepo or a collection of finer-grained repositories. The specific decisions of how to store your source code (or store your files, for that matter) are easily debatable, and in some cases, the particulars of your organization and your workflow are going to matter more than others. These are decisions you will need to make yourself.

一套非常相似的问题，决定了应当偏好单体仓库、还是一组更细粒度的仓库。如何存储源代码（或就此而言，如何存储文件）的具体决策，很容易引发争论；在某些情况下，你组织与工作流的具体情形会比其他因素更重要。这些是你需要自己做出的决策。

What is important is not whether we focus on monorepo; it is to adhere to the One-Version principle to the greatest extent possible: developers must not have a choice when adding a dependency onto some library that is already in use in the organization. Choice violations of the One-Version Rule lead to merge strategy discussions, diamond dependencies, lost work, and wasted effort.

重要的不是我们是否聚焦于单体仓库；而是尽最大可能遵守“单一版本”原则：当开发者向某个已在组织中使用的库添加依赖时，绝不应有选择。对“单一版本规则”的选择式违反，会导致合并策略之争、菱形依赖、工作丢失与精力浪费。

原书第 373 页

Software engineering tools including both VCS and build systems are increasingly providing mechanisms to smartly blend between fine-grained repositories and monorepos to provide an experience akin to the monorepo—an agreed-upon ordering of commits and understanding of the dependency graph. Git submodules, Bazel with external dependencies, and CMake subprojects all allow modern developers to synthesize something weakly approximating monorepo behavior without the costs and downsides of a monorepo. For instance, fine-grained repositories are easier to deal with in terms of scale (Git often has performance issues after a few million commits and tends to be slow to clone when repositories include large binary artifacts) and storage (VCS metadata can add up, especially if you have binary artifacts in your version control system). Fine-grained repositories in a federated/virtual-monorepo (VMR)–style repository can make it easier to isolate experimental or top-secret projects while still holding to One Version and allowing access to common utilities.

包括 VCS 与构建系统在内的软件工程工具，正越来越多地提供机制，在细粒度仓库与单体仓库之间智能融合，以提供一种类似于单体仓库的体验——一套约定好的提交顺序与对依赖图的理解。Git 子模块、带外部依赖的 Bazel、以及 CMake 子项目，都让现代开发者能够合成出一种粗略近似单体仓库行为的东西，而无需承担单体仓库的成本与缺点。例如，细粒度仓库在规模上更容易处理（Git 在几百万次提交后常有性能问题，当仓库包含大型二进制制品时克隆往往很慢），在存储上也更易处理（VCS 元数据会累积，尤其当你的版本控制系统里有二进制制品时）。联邦式/虚拟单体仓库（VMR）风格仓库中的细粒度仓库，可以更容易地隔离实验性或绝密项目，同时仍坚持“单一版本”、并允许访问公共工具。

To put it another way: if every project in your organization has the same secrecy, legal, privacy, and security requirements, a true monorepo is a fine way to go. Otherwise, aim for the functionality of a monorepo, but allow yourself the flexibility of implementing that experience in a different fashion. If you can manage with disjoint repositories and adhere to One Version or your workload is all disconnected enough to allow truly separate repositories, great. Otherwise, synthesizing something like a VMR in some fashion may represent the best of both worlds. After all, your choice of filesystem format really does not matter as much as what you write to it.

换句话说：如果你组织中的每个项目都有相同的保密、法律、隐私与安全要求，那么一个真正的单体仓库是个不错的选择。否则，就追求单体仓库的功能，但允许自己以不同方式实现那种体验的灵活性。如果你能用互不相交的仓库应付、并坚持“单一版本”，或者你的工作负载彼此足够独立、以至于可以使用真正分离的仓库，那很好。否则，以某种方式合成一个类似 VMR 的东西，可能兼具两者之长。毕竟，你选择哪种文件系统格式，真的不如你往里面写什么来得重要。

Future of Version Control · 版本控制的未来

Google is not the only organization to publicly discuss the benefits of a monorepo approach. Microsoft, Facebook, Netflix, and Uber have also publicly mentioned their reliance on the approach. DORA has published about it extensively. It is vaguely possible that all of these successful, long-lived companies are misguided, or at least that their situations are sufficiently different as to be inapplicable to the average smaller organization. Although it is possible, we think it is unlikely.

Google 并不是唯一公开讨论单体仓库做法好处的组织。Microsoft、Facebook、Netflix 和 Uber 也都公开提到过它们对这一做法的依赖。DORA 对此有大量出版物。要说所有这些成功、长寿的公司都被误导了，或者至少它们的情形差异大到不适用于一般的小型组织，这种可能性并非完全没有。尽管有可能，但我们认为不大可能。

Most arguments against monorepos focus on the technical limitations of having a single large repository. If cloning a repository from upstream is quick and cheap, developers are more likely to keep changes small and isolated (and to avoid making

反对单体仓库的大多数论点，聚焦于拥有单个大型仓库的技术局限。如果从上游克隆仓库又快又便宜，开发者更可能把改动保持得小而孤立（也更能避免把

原书第 374 页

mistakes with committing to the wrong work-in-progress branch). If cloning a repository (or doing some other common VCS operation) takes hours of wasted developer time, you can easily see why an organization would shy away from reliance on such a large repository/operation. We luckily avoided this pitfall by focusing on providing a VCS that scales massively.

错误提交到错误的在制品分支）。如果克隆一个仓库（或做其他常见 VCS 操作）要浪费开发者数小时，你很容易理解为什么一个组织会回避依赖如此大的仓库/操作。我们幸运地通过专注于提供一个可大规模扩展的 VCS 而避开了这个陷阱。

Looking at the past few years of major improvements to Git, there is clearly a lot of work being done to support larger repositories: shallow clones, sparse branches, better optimization, and more. We expect this to continue and the importance of but we need to keep the repository small to diminish.

看看过去几年 Git 的重大改进，显然有大量工作在支持更大的仓库：浅克隆、稀疏分支、更好的优化等等。我们预计这一趋势会持续，“但我们需要保持仓库小”这种说法的重要性将会减弱。

The other major argument against monorepos is that it does not match how development happens in the Open Source Software (OSS) world. Although true, many of the practices in the OSS world come (rightly) from prioritizing freedom, lack of coordination, and lack of computing resources. Separate projects in the OSS world are effectively separate organizations that happen to be able to see one another's code. Within the boundaries of an organization, we can make more assumptions: we can assume the availability of compute resources, we can assume coordination, and we can assume that there is some amount of centralized authority.

反对单体仓库的另一个主要论点是：它与开源软件（OSS）世界中开发发生的方式不匹配。这话不假，但 OSS 世界的许多做法（理所当然地）来自把自由、缺乏协调、以及计算资源匮乏放在优先位置。OSS 世界中分离的项目，实际上是各自独立的组织，只是恰好能够看到彼此的代码。在一个组织的边界之内，我们可以做出更多假设：可以假设计算资源可用，可以假设存在协调，也可以假设有某种程度的中央权威。

A less common but perhaps more legitimate concern with the monorepo approach is that as your organization scales up, it is less and less likely that every piece of code is subject to exactly the same legal, compliance, regulatory, secrecy, and privacy requirements. One native advantage of a manyrepo approach is that separate repositories are obviously capable of having different sets of authorized developers, visibility, permissions, and so on. Stitching that feature into a monorepo can be done but implies some ongoing carrying costs in terms of customization and maintenance.

对单体仓库做法一种较少见、但或许更正当的担忧是：随着组织扩大，每一段代码都受到完全相同的法律、合规、监管、保密与隐私要求约束的可能性越来越小。多仓库做法的一个天然优势是：分离的仓库显然能够拥有不同的授权开发者集合、可见性、权限等等。把那项特性缝进一个单体仓库是可以做到的，但意味着在定制与维护方面会有一些持续的携带成本。

At the same time, the industry seems to be inventing lightweight interrepository linkage over and over again. Sometimes, this is in the VCS (Git submodules) or the build system. So long as a collection of repositories have a consistent understanding of what is trunk, which change happened first, and mechanisms to describe dependencies, we can easily imagine stitching together a disparate collection of physical repositories into one larger VMR. Even though Piper has done very well for us, investing in a highly scaling VMR and tools to manage it and relying on off-the-shelf customization for per-repository policy requirements could have been a better investment.

与此同时，行业似乎在一次次重新发明轻量级的跨仓库链接。有时这发生在 VCS 中（Git 子模块），有时发生在构建系统中。只要一组仓库对“什么是主干”“哪个变更先发生”以及描述依赖的机制有一致理解，我们很容易想象把一组各不相同的物理仓库缝合成一个更大的 VMR。尽管 Piper 对我们而言表现出色，但投资于一个高度可扩展的 VMR 及管理它的工具、并在每个仓库的政策要求上依赖现成的定制，或许曾是一笔更好的投资。

As soon as someone builds a sufficiently large nugget of compatible and interdependent projects in the OSS community and publishes a VMR view of those packages, we suspect that OSS developer practices will begin to change. We see glimpses of this in the tools that could synthesize a virtual monorepo as well as in the work done by (for instance) large Linux distributions discovering and publishing mutually compatible revisions of thousands of packages. With unit tests, CI, and automatic version bumping for new submissions to one of those revisions, enabling a package owner to

一旦有人在 OSS 社区中构建出一块足够大的、相互兼容且相互依赖的项目群，并发布这些包的 VMR 视图，我们预计 OSS 开发者的做法将开始改变。我们在那些能够合成虚拟单体仓库的工具中，以及（例如）大型 Linux 发行版发现并发布数千个包相互兼容修订版的工作中，已经看到了这一点的端倪。配合单元测试、CI，以及向其中某个修订提交新内容时的自动版本提升，让包所有者能够

原书第 375 页

update trunk for their package (in nonbreaking fashion, of course), we think that model will catch on in the open source world. It is just a matter of efficiency, after all: a (virtual) monorepo approach with a One-Version Rule cuts down the complexity of software development by a whole (difficult) dimension: time.

为自己的包更新主干（当然以不破坏的方式），我们认为那种模型会在开源世界流行开来。毕竟这只是效率问题：带“单一版本规则”的（虚拟）单体仓库做法，把软件开发的复杂度削减了一整个（困难的）维度：时间。

We expect version control and dependency management to evolve in this direction in the next 10 to 20 years: VCSs will focus on allowing larger repositories with better performance scaling, but also removing the need for larger repositories by providing better mechanisms to stitch them together across project and organizational boundaries. Someone, perhaps the existing package management groups or Linux distributors, will catalyze a de facto standard virtual monorepo. Depending on the utilities in that monorepo will provide easy access to a compatible set of dependencies as one unit. We will more generally recognize that version numbers are timestamps, and that allowing version skew adds a dimensionality complexity (time) that costs a lot—and that we can learn to avoid. It starts with something logically like a monorepo.

我们预计未来 10 到 20 年，版本控制与依赖管理将朝这个方向演进：VCS 将聚焦于支持更大的仓库、并取得更好的性能扩展，同时也会通过提供更好的机制、跨项目与组织边界把仓库缝在一起，来消除对更大仓库的需要。某个角色——也许是现有的包管理组织，或 Linux 发行商——将催化出一个事实标准的虚拟单体仓库。依赖那个单体仓库中的工具，将能把一整套兼容依赖作为一个单元轻松获取。我们将更普遍地认识到：版本号就是时间戳，允许版本偏移会增加一个维度的复杂度（时间），代价高昂——而我们可以学会避免它。它从某种逻辑上类似单体仓库的东西开始。

Conclusion · 小结

Version control systems are a natural extension of the collaboration challenges and opportunities provided by technology, especially shared compute resources and computer networks. They have historically evolved in lockstep with the norms of software engineering as we understand them at the time.

版本控制系统，是技术（尤其是共享计算资源与计算机网络）所带来的协作挑战与机遇的自然延伸。历史上，它们与我们当时所理解的软件工程规范同步演进。

Early systems provided simplistic file-granularity locking. As typical software engineering projects and teams grew larger, the scaling problems with that approach became apparent, and our understanding of version control changed to match those challenges. Then, as development increasingly moved toward an OSS model with distributed contributors, VCSs became more decentralized. We expect a shift in VCS technology that assumes constant network availability, focusing more on storage and build in the cloud to avoid transmitting unnecessary files and artifacts. This is increasingly critical for large, long-lived software engineering projects, even if it means a change in approach compared to simple single-dev/single-machine programming projects. This shift to cloud will make concrete what has emerged with DVCS approaches: even if we allow distributed development, something must still be centrally recognized as the Source of Truth.

早期系统提供简单的文件级锁定。随着典型软件工程项目与团队变大，那种做法的规模化问题变得明显，我们对版本控制的理解也随之改变以匹配那些挑战。随后，随着开发日益转向带分布式贡献者的 OSS 模式，VCS 变得更加去中心化。我们预计 VCS 技术将发生一次转向：假设网络始终可用，更聚焦于在云端存储与构建，以避免传输不必要的文件与制品。这对大型、长寿的软件工程项目日益关键，哪怕与简单的单开发者/单机编程项目相比它意味着做法上的改变。这次向云端的转向，将把 DVCS 做法中已经浮现的东西变得具体：即便我们允许分布式开发，也必须有某个东西在中央被承认为真相之源。

The current DVCS decentralization is a sensible reaction of the technology to the needs of the industry (especially the open source community). However, DVCS configuration needs to be tightly controlled and coupled with branch management policies that make sense for your organization. It also can often introduce unexpected scaling problems: perfect fidelity offline operation requires a lot more local data. Failure to rein in the potential complexity of a branching free-for-all can lead to a potentially unbounded amount of overhead between developers and deployment of that code. However, complex technology does not need to be used in a complex fashion: as

当前 DVCS 的去中心化，是技术对行业（尤其是开源社区）需求的一种合理反应。然而，DVCS 配置需要被严格控制，并与适合你组织的分支管理政策相结合。它也常常会引入意料之外的规模化问题：完美保真的离线操作需要多得多的本地数据。若不能管住“分支混战”的潜在复杂度，可能会在开发者与该代码的部署之间造成潜在无界的开销。然而，复杂的技术并不需要以复杂的方式使用：正如

原书第 376 页

we see in monorepo and trunk-based development models, keeping branch policies simple generally leads to better engineering outcomes.

我们在单体仓库与基于主干的开发模型中所看到的那样，保持分支政策简单，通常会带来更好的工程成果。

Choice leads to costs here. We highly endorse the One-Version Rule presented here: developers within an organization must not have a choice where to commit, or which version of an existing component to depend upon. There are few policies we are aware of that can have such an impact on the organization: although it might be annoying for individual developers, in the aggregate, the end result is far better.

选择在此会带来成本。我们高度赞同这里提出的“单一版本规则”：组织内的开发者，在“提交到哪里”或“依赖既有组件的哪个版本”上绝不应有选择。我们所知的、能对组织产生如此影响的政策寥寥无几：尽管它对个体开发者可能有些烦人，但总体而言，最终结果要好得多。

TL;DRs · 本章要点

  • Use version control for any software development project larger than toy project with only one developer that will never be updated.

    对任何比“只有一名开发者、永远不会更新的玩具项目”更大的软件开发项目，都使用版本控制。

  • There is an inherent scaling problem when there are choices in which version of this should I depend upon?

    当“我该依赖这个的哪个版本？”存在选择时，会存在固有的规模化问题。

  • One-Version Rules are surprisingly important for organizational efficiency. Removing choices in where to commit or what to depend upon can result in significant simplification.

    单一版本规则对组织效率的重要性出人意料。消除“提交到哪里”“依赖什么”上的选择，可以带来显著的简化。

  • In some languages, you might be able to spend some effort to dodge this with technical approaches like shading, separate compilation, linker hiding, and so on. The work to get those approaches working is entirely lost labor—your software engineers are not producing anything, they are just working around technical debts.

    在某些语言中，你或许能花些力气，用 shading、单独编译、链接器隐藏等技术手段来回避这一点。让这些做法跑起来所付出的工作，完全是白费力气——你的软件工程师没有在产出任何东西，只是在绕开技术债。

  • Previous research (DORA/State of DevOps/Accelerate) has shown that trunk-based development is a predictive factor in high-performing development organizations. Long-lived dev branches are not a good default plan.

    先前的研究（DORA/DevOps 现状报告/Accelerate）已表明：基于主干的开发是高绩效开发组织的一个预测因子。长期 dev 分支不是一个好的默认方案。

  • Use whatever version control system makes sense for you. If your organization wants to prioritize separate repositories for separate projects, it is still probably wise for interrepository dependencies to be unpinned/at head/trunk based. There are an increasing number of VCS and build system facilities that allow you to have both small, fine-grained repositories as well as a consistent virtual head/trunk notion for the whole organization.

    使用任何对你有意义的版本控制系统。如果你的组织希望为不同项目优先使用分离的仓库，那么跨仓库依赖仍以“不锁定/处于 head/基于主干”为明智之举。越来越多的 VCS 与构建系统设施，让你既能拥有小而细粒度的仓库，又能为整个组织拥有一个一致的虚拟 head/主干概念。
